cards.text:
What is the most common cause of small bowel obstruction?
{{c1::Adhesion}}

Does achalasia present with dysphagia for solids or liquids?
{{c1::Both solids and liquids :)}}
cards.extra:
important distinguishing feature from obstruction (solids only)
This leads to putrid breath

cards.text: {{c1::Ascending cholangitis}} is a bacterial infection of the {{c2::bile ducts}}
cards.extra: bacteria can "ascend" from the duodenum due to inability of bile to "wash out" the ducts

cards.text: Obstructive jaundice is associated with {{c1::steatorrhea::GI symptom}}, with malabsorption of fat-soluble vitamins
cards.extra: decreased bile in the duodenum results in reduced ability to digest fat

cards.text: Meckel diverticulum is associated with the "rule of {{c1::2s}}"
{{c1::Cardiospasm}} is a spasm of the musculature of the cardia or epicardia that may produce partial or complete obstruction to the passage of food into the stomach
Acute pancreatitis is most commonly due to {{c1::alcohol}} or {{c2::gallstones}}
cards.extra: alcohol causes contraction of sphincter of Oddi; gallstones block drainage (duct of Wirsung)

cards.text: The most common causes of squamous cell carcinoma of the esophagus are {{c1::alcohol}} and {{c2::tobacco}}
Serrated colonic polyps may develop into CRC via {{c1::CpG}} hypermethylation with microsatellite instability and mutations in {{c2::BRAF}}
cards.extra:
- these colorectal cancers are known as having a CIMP phenotype (CpG island methylator phenotype)
- Hypermethylation may silence Mismatch Repair as it tricks MMR into thinking mutations in BRAF are on the old strand as opposed to the new strand
up to 20% of cases of sporadic CRC, can also be inherited (HNPCC syndrome)

cards.text: Most cases of diffuse gastric cancer are due to {{c1::E-cadherin}} mutations
An exophytic mass with bleeding and ulcerations is the characteristic gross appearance of {{c1::intestinal::diffuse/intestinal}}-type gastric adenocarcinoma
Hirschsprung disease is characterized by massive dilation of the bowel {{c1::proximal::proximal or distal}} to the aganglionic segment, resulting in a "transition zone"
{{c2::Necrotizing enterocolitis}} is a GI pathology seen in premature, {{c1::formula}}-fed infants with immature immune systems
cards.extra:
secondary to GI and immune immaturity, upon initiation of enteral feeding, bacteria are introduced to bowel where they proliferate excessively due to compromised immune clearance; impaired mucosal barrier function allows the bacteria to invade the bowel wall, causing inflammation and ischemic necrosis of the terminal ileum and colon
as the disease progresses, bowel becomes congested and gangrenous with formation of intramural gas collections; up to 30% of affected neonates die, esp. when disease is complicated by intestinal perf; survivors are at risk for strictures and bowel obstruction

cards.text:
Does viral hepatitis result in unconjugated or conjugated hyperbilirubinemia?
{{c1::Both :)}}
cards.extra: due to damage to both hepatocytes (UCB) and small bile ductules (CB)

cards.text: Duodenal ulcers located in the {{c1::posterior}} duodenum may rupture, leading to bleeding from the {{c2::gastroduodenal}} artery
cards.extra: also may lead to acute pancreatitis

cards.text: Achalasia is characterized by uncoordinated or absent {{c1::peristalsis}} in the esophagus

Which liver mass is benign yet carries a small risk (~10%) of transformation to hepatocellular carcinoma?
{{c1::Hepatic adenomas}}

Small bowel obstruction is less commonly due to what?
{{c1::Tumor (e.g. cancer)}}
Gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) often presents with {{c1::heartburn}}, which can mimic cardiac chest pain

What type of hernia increases risk of developing GERD?
{{c1::Sliding hiatal hernia}}
cards.extra: other risk factors for GERD include alcohol, tobacco, obesity, fat-rich diet, and caffeine

cards.text: Symptoms of esophageal carcinoma include progressive {{c1::dysphagia (solids to liquids)}}, weight loss, pain, and hematemesis

Loss of which hormones/neurotransmitters are implicated in the pathogenesis of achalasia?
{{c1::NO and VIP::2}}
cards.extra: increased LES tone due to decreased relaxation

cards.text:
What are modifiable risk factors for gastric adenocarcinoma?
{{c1::Smoking and Alcohol::2}}
Achlorhydria can result inabdominal discomfort, diarrhea, malabsorption, {{c1::iron deficiency}} anemia and infections by {{c2::vibrio}} species
cards.extra:
Iron deficiency because acid helps facilitate the absorption of iron; acid helps defend against ingested bacteria, thus loss of stomach acid allows for uncommon infections of organisms found in food
vibrio spp. are very acid sensitive

cards.text: Pancreatic insufficiency is associated with {{c1::decreased}} duodenal pH
cards.extra: secondary to decreased bicarbonate secretion

cards.text: Hyperplastic colonic polyps are usually {{c2::small::size}} and located in the {{c1::rectosigmoid}} region

Which type of esophageal cancer (SCC or adenocarcinoma) is associated with very hot tea?
{{c1::Squamous cell carcinoma}}
Gastric carcinoma typically presents {{c1::late::timing}} with weight loss, early satiety, abdominal pain, and anemia
Ménétrier disease is a premalignant stomach enteropathy characterized by massive gastric folds associated with excessive {{c1::transforming growth factor alpha (TGF-α)}}

Does H. pylori invade the stomach mucosa?
{{c1::No (sits on top of mucosa)}}
GI tract diverticula classically arise where the {{c1::vasa recta}} perforates the {{c2::muscularis externa}} (weak point in colonic wall)
{{c2::Meckel}} diverticulum is diagnosed using a(n) {{c1::99mTc-pertechnetate}} study for uptake by heterotopic gastric mucosa
cards.extra: heterotopic = presence of ectopic tissue plus retention of original tissue type; increased uptake of 99mTc-pertechnetate in the periumbilical / RLQ is characteristic of Meckel diverticulum

cards.text: {{c2::Gastric}} ulcers present with epigastric pain that {{c1::worsens}} with meals
cards.extra: and can therefore lead to weight loss

cards.text: {{c2::Mallory-Weiss}} syndrome is a linear {{c1::mucosal}} laceration at the gastroesophageal (GE) junction

What is the most common classification of gastric carcinoma (e.g. SCC, lymphoma, adenocarcinoma, etc.)?
{{c1::Adenocarcinoma}}
cards.extra: less commonly lymphoma, GI stromal tumor, or carcinoid tumor

cards.text: {{c1::Abetalipoproteinemia}} is associated with absent plasma VLDL and LDL, which require apoB-100
Perforation of an anterior duodenal ulcer may present with referred pain to the {{c1::shoulder}} via the phrenic nerve
cards.extra: due to irritation of the diaphragm

cards.text:
Which type of gastric carcinoma (intestinal or diffuse) is associated with H. pylori infection?
{{c1::Intestinal}}

Bowel ischemia and necrosis is most susceptible to the {{c1::superficial mucosa (with villi)::which layer?}} of the GI tract
*bonus: why?
cards.extra: * Because arteries become smaller as they move toward the luminal surface of the bowel

cards.text: Gastric carcinoma is subclassified into {{c1::intestinal}} and {{c2::diffuse}} types
{{c1::Benign::Benign or Malignant}} gastric ulcers are usually small (< 3 cm), sharply demarcated ("punched-out"), and surrounded by radiating folds of mucosa
Complications associated with {{c2::Crohn disease}} (IBD) include gallstones and {{c1::calcium oxalate}} nephrolithiasis
cards.extra:
- Crohns almost always affect the terminal ileum (where bile salts are reabsorbed) --> fatty acid malabsorption (ADEK deficiency)
- increased intestinal fat binds Ca2+, thus, less Ca2+ is available to bind oxalate, leading to increased oxalate absorption

cards.text: Cholangiocarcinoma obstructing the biliary tree may present with {{c1::light::color}} stoolsand{{c1::dark::color}} urine
cards.extra:
* back up of bile into liver -> leaks through tight junctions -> conjugated bilirubin in the blood -> filtered in the kidneys in the urine (dark urine)
* Urobiligen not secreted into small intestine -> bacteria don't have urobiligen to make stercobilin-> lack of stercobilin in feces -> light stool

cards.text:
Does eosinophilic esophagitis respond to GERD therapy (e.g. PPIs)?
{{c1::No}}
cards.extra: However, a 2-month trial of PPIs is part of the diagnostic evaluation; if there is no symptom improvement, an endoscopy with esophageal biopsy is warranted

cards.text: Squamous cell carcinoma of the esophagus may present with {{c1::hoarseness}} due to involvement of the recurrent laryngeal nerve
{{c1::Acute mesenteric ischemia}} is associated with small bowel necrosis and abdominal pain out of proportion to physical findings
cards.extra: other features include bloody diarrhea and decreased bowel sounds

cards.text: {{c3::Pancreatic adenocarcinoma}} often presents as obstructive {{c1::jaundice}} with a(n) {{c2::painless}}, palpable gallbladder
cards.extra:
Courvoisier sign; occurs with tumors that arise in the head of pancreas (most common location)
Painless because this is a chronic condition, head chronically obstructs bile duct and bile flow backs up and distend gallbladder over time (no acute distension)

cards.text: Hemorrhoids may occur in {{c1::pregnant women::demographic}} due to increased intra-abdominal pressure and IVC compression
cards.extra: * leads to venous pooling and engorgement

cards.text: {{c2::Gastric}} adenocarcinoma rarely may present with the {{c1::Leser-Trélat}} sign, which is sudden onset of multiple {{c3::seborrheic keratoses}}

What is the likely diagnosis in a diabetic patient with anorexia, postprandial bloating/vomiting, and early satiety without heartburn or epigastric pain?
{{c1::Gastroparesis}}
The {{c2::microsatellite}} instability pathway of colorectal cancer is characterized by mutations or methylation of {{c1::mismatch repair}} genes
cards.extra: e.g. MLH1, MSH2

cards.text:
Which type of gastric carcinoma (diffuse or intestinal) is associated with Krukenberg tumor?
{{c1::Diffuse}}
cards.extra: thus Krukenberg tumor is characterized by abundant mucin-secreting, signet ring cells

cards.text: Esophageal carcinoma in the middle third of the esophagus spreads to {{c1::mediastinal}}, {{c2::tracheobronchial}}, or {{c3::paratracheal}} lymph nodes
{{c1::Barrett's esophagus}} is characterized by specialized intestinal metaplasia of the lower esophageal mucosa
Foods containing N-nitroso compounds increase the risk for esophageal {{c1::squamous cell carcinoma}}
cards.extra: * e.g. pickled vegetables, preserved meats; due to irritant effect

cards.text: A(n) {{c1::Blumer shelf}} is a palpable rectal mass suggesting metastasis to the rectouterine pouch from a(n) {{c2::gastric}} malignancy
Gastric {{c1::ulcers::erosions or ulcers}} may extend into and beyond the {{c2::submucosa}}
cards.extra: e.g. submucosa, muscularis externa

cards.text: Acute pancreatitis may progress to {{c1::shock}}, due to pancreatic hemorrhage and fluid sequestration

Which type of gastric carcinoma (intestinal or diffuse) is more common?
{{c1::Intestinal}}
{{c1::Ménétrier}} disease is characterized by hypertrophied gastric rugae that resemble brain gyri
{{c2::Celiac}} disease is associated with {{c1::dermatitis herpetiformis}}, which are small, herpes-like vesicles on the skin
cards.extra: due to cross-reactivity between anti-gliadin IgA antibodies and transglutaminase at the dermal basement membrane

cards.text: {{c1::Squamous cell carcinoma}} of the esophagus is the most common type of esophageal carcinoma {{c2::worldwide::location}}
{{c1::Eosinophilic esophagitis}} is characterized by eosinophilic infiltration of the esophagus, often in {{c2::atopic}} patients
{{c1::Gallstone}} ileus occurs secondary to cholecystitis with fistula formation between the {{c2::gallbladder}} and {{c3::small bowel}}
cards.extra:
results in pneumobilia (air in biliary tree), crampy pain, vomiting, bloating; signs of small bowel obstruction (abdominal distension, tenderness, high-pitched bowel sounds)
pneumobilia occurs due to retrograde passage of intestinal gas through fistula

cards.text: Wilson disease results in lack of copper transport into {{c1::bile}} and lack of incorporation into {{c2::ceruloplasmin}}
cards.extra:
copper thus builds up in hepatocytes, leaks into serum, and deposits in tissues
Goljan: TOTAL copper level is decreased (due to lower ceruloplasmin), but FREE copper level is increased

cards.text: Ménétrier disease is characterized by excess mucus production with resultant {{c1::protein}} loss, leading to edema
cards.extra:
thus also referred to as hypoproteinemic hypertrophic gastropathy
↑ mucus neutralizes acid of stomach
↑ mucus carries protein out (leads to edema/facial swelling due to hypoalbuminemia)

cards.text:
Which virus is a risk factor for gastric adenocarcinoma?
{{c1::Epstein-Barr virus}}
cards.extra: * in addition, EBV may cause gastric lymphomas

cards.text:
What increases the risk of esophageal adenocarcinoma especially with pre-existing Barrett's esophagus?
{{c1::Smoking}}
Patches of red velvety mucosa (columnar epithelium) extending upward form the gastroesophageal junction is seen in {{c1::Barrett's esophagus}}
Achalasia is characterized by {{c1::high}} LES pressure on esophageal manometry
cards.extra: important distinguishing feature from sclerodermal esophageal dysmotility

cards.text:
Which biliary tract disease is classically seen in middle-aged women and presents with generalized pruritis and fatigue?
{{c1::Primary biliary cholangitis (PBC)}}
cards.extra: May present with signs of fat soluble vitamin deficiency; signs of cholestasis (visible jaundice, pale stool, dark urine) and hypercholesterolemia (xanthelasma) is often not apparent until later in the disease course

cards.text: Esophageal web presents with dysphagia for {{c1::poorly chewed}} food

What is the most common cause of esophageal perforation (e.g. Boerhaave syndrome)?
{{c1::Iatrogenic (especially endoscopy)}}

The causes of {{c14::acute pancreatitis}} may be remembered with the mnemonic "I GET PP SMASHED":
I: {{c1::Idiopathic}}
G: {{c2::Gallstones}}
E: {{c3::Ethanol}}
T: {{c4::Trauma (e.g. automobile accident in children - seatbelt injury)}}
P: {{c13::Posterior duodenal ulcer rupture}}
P: {{c15::Pancreas Divisum}}
S: {{c5::Steroids}}
M: {{c6::Mumps}}
A: {{c7::Autoimmune disease}}
S: {{c8::Scorpion sting}}
H: {{c9::HYPERcalcemia}} or {{c10::Hypertriglyceridemia/Hyperchylomicronemia}}
E: {{c11::ERCP (endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography)}}
D: {{c12::Drugs (e.g. sulfa drugs, NRTIs, protease inhibitors)}}
cards.extra:
G - Specifically at Ampulla of Vater
E - alcohol triggers release of pancreatic enzymes - also results in alcoholic liver disease, peripheral neuropathy, testicular atrophy
T - children being restrained by seatbelts
P - pancreas sits behind posterior duodenum - rupture perforates pancreas; Pancreas Divisum is an embryological cause; other structural abnormalities of the pancreatic duct (strictures, cancer) or the ampullary region (choledochal cyst, stenosis of sphincter of oddi)
M - mumps; other infections are coxsackievirus, mycoplasma pneumoniae
A - Typically due to IgG4 related disease (+ Riedel's thyroiditis, retroperitoneal fibrosis, noninfectious aortitis)
S - Scorpion stings (especially in Trinidad) + brown recluse spider + gila monster lizard; Surgery (particularly of the stomach and biliary tract and after cardiac surgery)
H - calcium deposits in pancreas ducts and activates trypsinogen ; chylomicrons obstruct pancreatic capillaries, lead to local ischemia - exposes TAGs to pancreatic lipases, leads to proinflam CK / free radicals --> tissue injury
D - Didanosine, Corticosteroids, Alcohol, Valproic Acid, Azathioprine, Furosemide, HCTZ, GLP-1 analogs, 6MP in addition

cards.text: Gastric ulcers on the lesser curvature of the stomach may rupture, leading to bleeding from the {{c1::left gastric}} artery
Sclerodermal esophageal dysmotility is characterized by {{c1::low}} LES pressure on esophageal manometry
cards.extra: important distinguishing feature from achalasia

cards.text:
Which area of the stomach is initially affected by chronic H. pylori gastritis?
{{c1::Antrum}}
cards.extra: eventually spread to body of the stomach

cards.text: Esophageal carcinoma is subclassified as {{c1::adenocarcinoma}} or {{c2::squamous cell carcinoma}}
{{c1::Squamous cell carcinoma}} of the esophagus is a malignant proliferation of squamous cells
Surgery, diabetes, drugs and sepsis are common causes of {{c1::ileus::what small bowel disorder?}}

What is the most common congenital anomaly of the GI tract?
{{c1::Meckel diverticulum}}
cards.extra: affects 2% of the population

cards.text:
What is the effect of chronic gastritis on gastric HCl secretion?
{{c1::Decreased (achlorhydria or hypochlorhydria)}}
cards.extra: due to atrophy of gastric mucosa and intestinal metaplasia

cards.text: {{c1::Lynch}} syndrome is due to an inherited defect in {{c2::DNA mismatch repair}} enzymes, resulting in microsatellite instability
{{c1::Adenocarcinoma}} of the esophagus is a malignant proliferation of glands
Gastric carcinoma may spread and involve the {{c1::bilateral ovaries}}, also known as a(n) {{c2::Krukenberg tumor}}
cards.extra: bilateral involvement is an important distinguishing feature from ovarian adenocarcinoma

cards.text: Small bowel obstruction may present with {{c1::colicky::description}} abdominal pain, nausea/vomiting, and *constipation
cards.extra: * due to inability to pass flatus or stool

cards.text: Meckel diverticulum is two times more likely to occur in {{c1::males::gender}}
Gastric carcinoma may spread and involve the {{c1::left supraclavicular}} node, also known as {{c2::Virchow's node}}
{{c2::Chronic}} pancreatitis is characterized by atrophy and dystrophic {{c1::calcification}} of pancreatic parenchyma on imaging
cards.extra: in alcohol related chronic pancreatitis, alcohol induces secretion of protein rich fluid; proteinaceous secretions precipitate within pancreatic ducts forming ductal plugs that may calcify

cards.text: Esophageal strictures are associated with {{c1::caustic ingestion}} and {{c2::GERD}}
cards.extra: <u>caustics</u> are strong acids and alkalis

cards.text: One possible ulcer complication is {{c1::obstruction}} of the pyloric channel or duodenum
{{c1::Malignant::Benign or Malignant}} gastric ulcers are usually large and irregular with heaped up margins

Acute {{c1::pancreatitis}} is diagnosed by 2 of 3 criteria:
- Acute epigastric pain that radiates to the back
- Increased serum amylase or lipase to 3x upper limit of normal
- Characteristic imaging findings
{{c2::Eosinophilic esophagitis}} presents with esophageal {{c1::rings}} and linear furrows, often seen on endoscopy
Gastric {{c1::erosions::erosions or ulcers}} involves loss of the {{c2::mucosal}} layer only

What is the likely diagnosis for a patient with atherosclerosis who presents with crampy postprandial epigastric pain, food aversion, and weight loss?
{{c1::Chronic mesenteric ischemia}}

Which type of gallstone (cholesterol or pigment) is associated with rapid weight loss?
{{c1::Cholesterol gallstone}}
cards.extra:
very low calorie diets with decreased caloric intake and rapid weight loss can lead to bile stasis and increased cholesterol mobilization
- e.g. patients with Roux-en-Y gastric bypass surgery (patients often receive prophylactic ursodeoxycholic acid for 6 months to reduce risk of gallstone development)
- weight loss causes body to secrete extra cholesterol into bile → ↑ risk for cholesterol stones

cards.text: Porcelain gallbladder is a shrunken, hard gallbladder due to chronic inflammation, fibrosis, and dystrophic {{c1::calcification}}
cards.extra: grossly, includes a bluish, brittle, thickened gallbladder "crunchy" texture; calcified plaques within the muscularis or spotty calcification in the mucosa

cards.text: The {{c2::intestinal}} type of gastric carcinoma is associated with {{c1::nitrosamines}}, which are found in smoked foods (common in Japan)
Temporary lactase deficiency may be seen after small bowel {{c1::infection (e.g. viral enteritis)}}
cards.extra: lactase is highly susceptible to injury

cards.text:
Does ménétrier disease increase risk for gastric cancer?
{{c1::Yes (pre-cancerous lesion)}}
Barrett esophagus is characterized by extension of the {{c1::squamocolumnar}} junction (Z-line) into the esophageal mucosa
Esophageal {{c2::varices}} are a common cause of death in patients with {{c1::cirrhosis}}
Small and large bowel ischemia initially spares {{c1::crypts}}, which contain secretory cells and {{c2::stem}} cells

How do platelet levels change with portal hypertension?
{{c1::Decreased}}
cards.extra: due to splenomegaly and splenic sequestration

cards.text: The {{c2::diffuse}} type of gastric carcinoma is characterized by {{c1::signet ring}} cells that infiltrate the gastric wall
cards.extra: signet ring cells are mucin-filled cells with peripheral nuclei

cards.text:
Which type of esophageal cancer (SCC or adenocarcinoma) is associated with achalasia?
{{c1::Both :)}}
cards.extra: note: pathoma only mentions SCC

cards.text:
Which form of IBD has increased risk for gallstones (both cholesterol and pigment)?
{{c1::Crohn disease}}
cards.extra: Usually affects the terminal ileum so less reuptake of bile acids/salts (which are necessary for cholesterol to solubilize in the bile)

cards.text:
What is the likely diagnosis in a patient with severe epigastric pain radiating to the back and peripancreatic edema/hemorrhage on CT?
{{c1::Acute necrotizing pancreatitis}}
Carcinoid tumors may arise anywhere in the gut, however, they most commonly arise in the {{c1::small bowel}}
cards.extra: grows a submucosal polyp-like nodule

cards.text: Gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) may damage the {{c1::enamel}} of teeth

What type of gastric adenocarcinoma displays disorganized cell growth throughout the stomach "infiltrative growth pattern"?
{{c1::Diffuse-type gastric adenocarcinoma}}
The {{c2::diffuse}} type of gastric carcinoma may cause {{c1::linitis plastica}}, which is a grossly thickened and leathery stomach wall
cards.extra: due to desmoplastic reaction in response to cancer infiltration

cards.text:
What are the treatments for Crigler-Najjar syndrome type I?
{{c1::Plasmapheresis and phototherapy::2}}
Meckel diverticulum arises due to persistence of the {{c1::vitelline (omphalomesenteric) duct}}
{{c1::Hirschsprung}} disease is characterized by defective relaxation and peristalsis of the rectum and distal sigmoid colon
cards.extra: Rectum and Anus are 100% involved, 75% of time in sigmoid colon

cards.text:
Which part of the esophagus is typically affected by adenocarcinoma?
{{c1::Lower 1/3rd}}

What is the most common skin malignancy in immunocompromised states and/or those with a chronic scar?
{{c1::Squamous cell carcinoma}}
cards.extra: * may be described as raised plaques with central ulceration

cards.text:
What type of gastric ulcer is caused by increased intracranial pressure?
{{c1::Cushing ulcer}}
cards.extra: "Always Cushion the brain"

cards.text: In Barrett's esophagus, {{c1::non-keratinized stratified squamous epithelium}} is replaced with {{c2::non-ciliated columnar epithelium with goblet cells}} (metaplasia)
cards.extra: response of lower esophageal stem cells to acidic stress

cards.text: Small bowel obstruction initially presents with {{c1::hyperactive (high pitched "tinkling")}} bowel sounds due to abdominal peristalsis
Peptic ulcer disease is a solitary mucosal ulcer involving the {{c1::proximal duodenum}} (90%) or {{c2::distal stomach}} (10%)
{{c2::Boerhaave}} syndrome is a(n) {{c1::transmural}} laceration of the distal esophagus

What type of colonic polyp is small (< 5 mm) and resembles normal mucosa?
{{c1::Mucosal polyps (clinically insignificant)}}
{{c1::Adenocarcinoma}} of the esophagus is the most common type of esophageal carcinoma in {{c2::America::location}}
{{c1::Diffuse esophageal spasm}} presents with spontaneous chest pain that radiates to the back, ears, and neck
{{c2::Achalasia}} is characterized by the "{{c1::Bird's beak}}" sign on barium swallow
cards.extra: dilated esophagus with an area of distal stenosis

cards.text: Betel nuts are a risk factor for {{c1::esophageal squamous cell carincoma}} due to irritant effect
{{c1::Perforation}} of an anterior duodenal ulcer is characterized by free air under the diaphragm (pneumoperitoneum)
The most common location for a pancreatic pseudocyst is in the {{c1::lesser peritoneal sac}}
cards.extra: bordered by the stomach, duodenum, and transverse colon

cards.text: The serotonin released from carcinoid tumors in the small bowel is metabolized in the {{c1::liver}} by {{c2::monoamine oxidase (MAO)}}, producing {{c3::5-HIAA}}
cards.extra: first-pass metabolism; serotonin travels to the liver via the portal vein

cards.text: {{c1::Chronic}} gastritis occurs due to chronic inflammation of the stomach mucosa
{{c1::Meckel}} diverticulum is an outpouching of all three layers of the bowel wall (true diverticulum)
The pathogenesis of Diffuse Esophageal Spasm likely involves impaired {{c1::inhibitory neurotransmission}} within the esophageal myenteric plexus

Which type of esophageal cancer (SCC or adenocarcinoma) is associated with esophageal web (e.g. Plummer-Vinson syndrome)?
{{c1::Squamous cell carcinoma}}
Air-fluid levels, "transition point", and epigastric distension are x-ray findings that may be seen in {{c1::small bowel obstruction::what GI pathology?}}
The IVC drains into the right atrium just above the level of the diaphragm at {{c1::T8}}
{{c1::Volvulus}} is caused by twisting of a portion of bowel around its mesentery

Which type of ulcer (gastric or duodenal) is more likely to be malignant?
{{c1::Gastric}}
cards.extra: duodenal carcinoma is extremely rare

cards.text: Pancreatitis (acute and chronic) may present with {{c1::epigastric}} abdominal pain that radiates to the {{c2::back}}
{{c3::Pleomorphic adenoma}} is a salivary gland tumor composed of {{c1::chondromyxoid stroma}} and {{c2::epithelium}}
cards.extra: composed of two different tissues, thus may be referred to as a "mixed" or "biphasic" tumor

cards.text: Diffuse esophageal spasm is associated with {{c1::GERD}}
cards.extra: attacks are often precipitated by ingestion of hot and cold liquids

cards.text: Obstructive jaundice is associated with {{c1::decreased}} urine urobilinogen
cards.extra: due to less bile entering the duodenum

cards.text: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma at the head of the pancreas may present with {{c1::dark::color}} urine and {{c1::pale::color}} stool
cards.extra: * due to obstruction of the common bile duct -> elevated conjugated bilirubin/decreased conjugated bilirubin in GI tract -> dark urine/light stool

cards.text: Patients with diffuse esophageal spasm typically present with {{c1::intermittent}} solid / liquid dysphagia
The intestinal type of gastric carcinoma most commonly arises on the {{c1::lesser curvature of the antrum}}
cards.extra: looks like an ulcer with raised margins

cards.text: Small bowel obstruction may present with a(n) {{c1::tympanitic::sound}} abdomen and distension due to backup of gas in the intestines
Chronic mesenteric ischemia is associated with {{c1::mucosal::mucosal or transmural}} infarction
On a barium swallow x-ray, patients with diffuse esophageal spasm are seen to have a "{{c1::corkscrew esophagus}}"

PBC and PSC may cause elevation of what lab values?
{{c1::ALP, GGT, conjugated hyperbilirubinemia, and immune proteins (IgM)::4}}
In portal hypertension, the {{c1::left gastric}} vein backs up into the esophageal vein, resulting in varices
{{c2::Anti-smooth muscle}} autoantibodies are associated with {{c1::autoimmune hepatitis type 1}}
cards.extra: Plasma cells are found

cards.text: Achalasia may be idiopathic or secondary to a known insult, such as {{c1::Chagas}} disease and extraesophageal malignancies
cards.extra: Chagas disease is caused by Trypanosoma cruzi infection

cards.text: {{c2::Celiac}} disease is immune-mediated damage of small bowel villi due to {{c1::gluten}} exposure
cards.extra: gluten is present in wheat and grains; also known as gluten-sensitive enteropathy and celiac sprue

cards.text:
What is the likely diagnosis for an adult with episodic, painless dark maroon-colored stool?
{{c1::Angiodysplasia}}
cards.extra: * associated with aortic arch stenosis, renal disease, and vWd

cards.text: {{c2::Hirschsprung}} disease occurs due to a congenital failure of {{c1::ganglion}} cells to descend into the myenteric and submucosal plexus
cards.extra: Ganglion cells are derived from the Neural Crest; neural crest cells moved caudally along vagal nerve fibers, present in wall of proximal colon at 8th week of gestation, and in rectum by 12th week

cards.text: Fibrous replacement of the muscularis in the lower esophagus is the cause of esophageal dysmotility in {{c1::CREST}} syndrome
Ménétrier disease presents with {{c1::epigastric}} pain, anorexia, weight loss, vomiting, and edema (due to {{c2::protein loss}})
Progression of colonic adenoma to carcinoma occurs with mutations in the {{c1::p53}} or loss of heterozygosity in the region that encodes for {{c2::SMAD}} 2 / 4
cards.extra: results in increased tumorigenesis; "AK-53": APC, KRAS, p53" ; DCC mutations are seen in ADVANCED colorectal cancer (ex stage IV)

cards.text: Mucosal defenses include secretion of {{c1::mucus}}, {{c2::HCO3-}}, prostaglandins, and {{c3::normal blood supply}}
cards.extra:
- Mucin layer is secreted by foveolar cells in the stomach
- bicarbonate is secreted by surface epithelium
- normal blood supply provides nutrients and picks up leaked acid

returns venous blood to the heart from the lower extremities, portal system, and abdominal and pelvic viscera
(seen here at level L1/L2 as observed by visible presence of renal arteries)

cards.text:
Which areas of the stomach are affected in chronic autoimmune gastritis?
{{c1::body and fundus}}
cards.extra: i.e. the location of parietal cells

cards.text: Peutz-Jeghers syndrome is associated with increased risk of {{c1::breast}}, {{c2::GI}}, and gynecologic cancers
cards.extra: e.g. colorectal, stomach, small bowel, pancreatic

cards.text: Squamous cell carcinoma of the esophagus may present with {{c1::cough}} due to tracheal involvement
{{c2::Appendicitis}} presents with diffuse periumbilical pain that eventually localizes to {{c1::McBurney's point}}
cards.extra:
also may present with fever and nausea
- afferent pain fibers for appendix / proximal colon / overlying visceral peritoneum cross through superior mesenteric plexus and enter spinal cord at T10 to produce vague referred pain to the umbilicus
- as the appendix becomes more inflamed, it itrritates the parietal peritoneum and abdominal wall to cause more severe somatic pain shifting from the initial referred umbilical pain to the McBurney's point

cards.text: Lynch syndrome, Peutz-Jeghers syndrome, Crohn's disease, and FAP are risk factors for small bowel {{c1::adenocarcinoma}}
cards.extra: * glandular cells with mucin will be seen on histology

cards.text: One sensitive sign of appendicitis and psoas abscess is the {{c1::psoas}} sign, which is pain on passive extension of the right hip
cards.extra: this is not specific as it can be due to any retroperitoneal irritation or inflammation of the psoas - not specific for appendicitis OR psoas abscess

cards.text: Portal {{c2::hypertension}} may lead to {{c1::portosystemic}} shunts, which can result in esophageal varices, gastric varices, anorectal varices, and caput medusae
cards.extra: also called portocaval shunts

cards.text:
Which gut wall layers are involved in a true diverticulum?
{{c1::All three (mucosa, submucosa, muscularis externa)}}
cards.extra: e.g. Meckel diverticulum OR traction diverticulosis, which is due to inflammation / subsequent scarring of gut wall, resulting in pulling / outpouching of all gut wall layers (ex midesophagus due to mediastinal lympadenitis caused by tuberculosis / fungal infection)

cards.text:
Is pancreatic insufficiency associated with normal or decreased urinary excretion of D-xylose (D-xylose test)?
{{c1::Normal}}
cards.extra: D-xylose is a monosaccharide that only depends on viable mucosa (not enzymatic breakdown) for absorption in the proximal small bowel. Excretion is decreased with mucosal defects and bacterial overgrowth

cards.text: Esophagitis may occur with medications such as {{c1::bisphosphonates}}, tetracyclines, NSAIDs, iron, and potassium chloride
{{c1::Black::color}} pigment gallstones are radio-{{c2::opaque}} and composed of {{c3::calcium bilirubinate}}
cards.extra: arise with hemolysis and ileal disease

cards.text:
Late complications of GERD include:
- {{c2::Barrett}} esophagus
- ulcerations followed by esophageal {{c1::strictures}}
cards.extra: presence of odynophagia (pain with swallowing) usually indicates the progression to erosive esophagitis and the formation of an ulcer (which can be confirmed with upper endoscopy)

cards.text:
Which part of the esophagus is typically affected by squamous cell carcinoma?
{{c1::Upper 2/3rds}}
Meckel diverticulum typically presents during the first two {{c1::years}} of life

What surgical procedure involves the en bloc removal of the head/neck of the pancreas, proximal duodenum, and gallbladder?
{{c1::Whipple procedure}}
cards.extra: used to treat pancreatic adenocarcinoma

cards.text: Acute mesenteric ischemia may present with "{{c1::currant jelly}}" stool

Peutz-Jeghers syndrome is a risk factor for what small bowel complications?
1. {{c1::Small bowel adenocarcinoma}}
2. {{c1::Small bowel obstruction}}
Lynch syndrome is usually right-sided and always involves the {{c1::proximal::proximal or distal}} colon

Is Meckel diverticulum a true or false diverticulum?
{{c1::True (outpouching of all layers)}}

What is the most common site for small bowel adenocarcinomas?
{{c1::Duodenum}}
Intussusception is most common in patients under {{c1::2}} years old
cards.extra: in these patients, it is often occurs without any structural cause;in those older than 2 years of age - a lead point should be sought (ex. a Meckel)

cards.text: {{c1::Juvenile polyposis}} syndrome is characterized by many juvenile polyps in the stomach, colon, and small bowel
cards.extra: class: may cause massive hemorrhage and thus children will need a colectomy

cards.text: Behçet syndrome occurs due to immune-complex {{c1::vasculitis}} involving primarily small vessels
cards.extra: Due to Th17 dysfunction and associated with HLA-B51

cards.text:
What drug class may be used to impede progression of colonic adenoma to
carcinoma?
{{c1::NSAIDs (e.g. aspirin)}}
cards.extra: due to decreased COX-2 expression

cards.text: Chronic gastritis is associated with {{c1::atrophy::hypertrophy or atrophy}} of the gastric mucosa
{{c1::Gastric::gastric or duodenal}} ulcers should be biopsied at the margins to rule out malignancy
cards.extra: duodenal / down malignancy

cards.text:
What lymph nodes are commonly affected in Whipple disease?
{{c1::Mesenteric nodes}}
Meckel diverticulum is typically two {{c1::inches}} long
{{c2::Achalasia}} is characterized by disordered esophageal motility due to inability to relax the {{c1::lower}} esophageal sphincter
cards.extra: A-chalasia = absence of relaxation

cards.text: Gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) may present with chronic cough and adult-onset {{c1::asthma}}
cards.extra: may also present with hoarseness (laryngopharyngeal reflux)

cards.text: {{c1::Gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD)}} is caused by reflux of acid from the stomach due to transiently decreased {{c2::LES}} tone
cards.extra: This is known as gastroesophageal junction incompetence

cards.text: Esophageal carcinoma in the lower third of the esophagus spreads to {{c1::celiac}} or {{c2::gastric}} lymph nodes
{{c2::Acute}} mesenteric ischemia may occur due to a thrombosis of the {{c1::mesenteric}} vein
{{c4::Zenker}} diverticulum classically arises at {{c1::Killian's triangle}}, between the {{c2::thyropharyngeal}} and {{c3::cricopharyngeal}} parts of the inferior pharyngeal constrictor
cards.extra: - this area is above the upper esophageal sphincter (aka the cricopharyngeal part), at the junction of the esophagus and pharynx (this area is a zone of muscle weakness)

cards.text:
What type of gastric ulcer is caused by severe burns?
{{c1::Curling ulcer}}
cards.extra: "Burned by the Curling iron" give PPIs to prevent

cards.text: Gastric {{c2::adenocarcinoma}} rarely may present with {{c1::acanthosis nigricans}}, which is hyperpigmented velvety plaques in the axilla and neck

How do platelet levels change with advanced liver disease?
{{c1::Decreased}}
cards.extra: due to decreased thrombopoietin and liver sequestration

cards.text: {{c1::Esophageal varices}} are dilated submucosal veins in the lower 1/3rd of the esophagus
{{c2::Duodenal}} ulcers present with epigastric pain that {{c1::improves}} with meals
cards.extra: due to increased HCO3- secretion in preparation for digestion
